about: Every material error found in our work, who or what produced it, how it was found and what changed. Register rule P10. The page transparency/performance-log.html is generated from this file by build/transparency/build_performance_log.py. Never edit an entry after it is written except to close it.

functions.Manager: Plans the work, routes it and holds the rules
functions.Data and analysis: Pulls official data, benchmarks, models and forecasts
functions.Scanning: Sweeps data releases, policy changes and forward dates
functions.Policy: Interprets policy and writes the policy products
functions.Verification: Fact-checks and reproduces work before it ships
functions.Not recorded: The record at the time did not say which function produced it

types.Source or edition: Wrong source, stale edition, or a fact taken from something other than the primary source
types.Unsupported claim: A statement the data or the source does not support
types.Data handling: A figure pulled, filtered or calculated wrongly
types.Completeness: Something that should have been covered was missed
types.Code or reference: A wrong geography code, dataset id, filter or identifier
types.Process: The wrong task, or a working rule not followed

stages.Published: Reached the site or a document sent out
stages.Draft: Reached Nathaniel in a draft, a working document or a chat answer, and stopped there
stages.Caught by checks: Caught by our own verification before it reached Nathaniel

entries.found_by: Full verification audit of every product
entries.what: Written commentary contradicted the data embedded in the same page. An inverted Whickham house-price claim, a false 'top half' sentence on the Explore Local Statistics scorecard, a reversed vacancies clause on the Employer Skills Survey dashboard and an unsupported policy claim
entries.fix: All four corrected on 15 July 2026. A check that re-reads every sentence of commentary against the final data was added to the dashboard publishing steps

entries.found_by: Full verification audit of every product
entries.what: The build script's NOMIS query for BRES left out the latest-date filter and took the first value returned, which was 2015. The map showed 98,000 employees where BRES 2024 gives 95,000
entries.fix: Script fixed at source on 28 July 2026 so it cannot recur on the monthly refresh

entries.what: An answer quoted a held scorecard figure for workplace pay (£590.10) labelled as ASHE 2025. A fresh pull the same day gave £670.30, below the North East, which reversed the point being made
entries.fix: Rule G7 written. Every figure comes from a fresh pull of the latest edition, or carries its true edition

entries.what: Deprivation ranks were quoted 'of 32,844', which is the 2019 count on 2011 boundaries. The 2025 indices rank 33,755 neighbourhoods
entries.fix: Corrected on 23 July 2026 and written into the rules as D5

entries.what: The instruction to complete outstanding actions was read as a verification report's open list rather than the production calendar. A whole session went on the wrong task and the overdue What's New was not produced that day
entries.fix: Rule G9 written. A small set of instructions now has a fixed meaning that is matched before anything is interpreted

entries.product: Weekly What's New, 3 August 2026 and later editions
entries.what: The Cabinet Statement 'Rewiring the State' of 31 July 2026 was reduced to a Budget-date item. Its non-fiscal half, on strategic authority rollout, boundary alignment, devolving by default and employment support, went unreported in every edition
entries.fix: Central government publications are now never filtered out, and every departmental feed item is listed in a complete log

entries.product: A labour market product in draft
entries.what: A draft explained wider Gateshead survey intervals by a cut to the Annual Population Survey sample boost. ONS documents a cut only to the Scottish boost
entries.fix: Removed before publication and written into rule D2

entries.product: Weekly What's New, editions to 8 September 2026
entries.found_by: Reconciliation against a fresh pull from gov.uk
entries.what: The departmental log was short by roughly half. The newsletter inbox script cut long emails partway through, so items such as MHCLG's review of local government reorganisation (7 September 2026) never reached the log. The log was checked only against the inbox, so the check kept passing
entries.fix: Truncation fixed on 8 September 2026. The gov.uk search API became the completeness check, and each edition states its counts

entries.found_by: Count check on the first build
entries.what: A wrong organisation identifier for MHCLG returned no rows and no error, so the log had no MHCLG items and still reconciled with itself
entries.fix: Both MHCLG identifiers are now queried, and every feed must return a non-zero count before the log is built

entries.found_by: Verification against the ONS geography register
entries.what: A correction on 29 July 2026 swapped the geography codes for Barnsley and Sheffield in a reference file. The dashboard carries the invalid code, so Barnsley is silently missing from two of its comparator groups
entries.fix: Reference files corrected on 18 September 2026 and rule D9 written. The dashboard itself still needs a full rebuild, which is deferred and tracked as an open defect

entries.what: A local skills plan's sector list was taken from press coverage of a different plan rather than from the plan itself
entries.fix: Rule G7a written. Policy facts and dates are quoted from the primary document, never from a search result or press summary

entries.what: A correctly sourced release date for UK Business Counts was changed to a wrong one on the strength of a dataset landing page, when the ONS release calendar had it confirmed
entries.fix: Rule G7a now says the release calendar is the authority on release dates

entries.what: Claims about other places were not traced to source. A figure was taken from a secondary account, growth rates could not be traced, and one place was called the 'only' one with results
entries.fix: Rule P8 written. Claims about other places pass a four-point check before they are used

entries.what: Four recommendations were for things that already existed, including a programme already commissioned for Gateshead and an evaluation already running to 2031
entries.fix: Rule P7 written. Existing provision is searched for before any recommendation is made

entries.what: The review was commissioned to improve the AI team's analysis but was read as advice to the council's team, so its lessons were written for the wrong reader
entries.fix: Rule G10 extended. Every review or recommendations brief names whose actions it recommends and who reads it

entries.product: Monthly Policy Update, August and September 2026
entries.what: Work on the income tax base was reported as outstanding in two editions, although it had been done on 31 July 2026
The edition said August's high streets package promised a consultation. It did not
The business department now publishes under a second organisation identifier. Querying the old one alone missed eight items, including the opening of the British Industrial Competitiveness Scheme
